pl-l4d8c7-d1e112.summary: States that the reality of this sacrament is twofold: one contained and signified, the flesh of Christ taken from the Virgin and the blood shed for us; the other signified and not contained, the unity of the Church in the predestined, called, justified, and glorified. This is Christ's twofold flesh.
claims: The eucharist contains and signifies Christ's flesh and blood.
It signifies but does not contain the unity of the Church.

pl-l4d8c7-d1e118.summary: Quotes Jerome: Christ's flesh and blood are understood in two ways: that which was crucified and buried and the blood shed by the soldier's lance, or the spiritual and divine flesh of which he says 'my flesh is truly food'.
claims: Christ's flesh is understood as his body and as spiritual flesh.

pl-l4d8c7-d1e127.summary: Distinguishes three things: what is sacrament only, the visible species of bread or wine; what is sacrament and reality, Christ's own flesh and blood; and what is reality and not sacrament, his mystical flesh.
claims: Christ's flesh and blood are sacrament and reality.
The mystical flesh is reality only.

pl-l4d8c7-d1e133.summary: Explains that the visible species is a sacrament of both realities, signifying each and bearing its likeness: as bread refreshes and sustains the body and wine gladdens and inebriates, Christ's flesh spiritually refreshes and nourishes the inner man more than other graces; and as one bread is made of many grains and wine flows together from many grapes, the Church's unity is made of many faithful.
claims: The species signify Christ's flesh and the Church's unity by likeness.

pl-l4d8c7-d1e140.summary: Cites Paul: we, though many, are one bread and one body.
claims: The many faithful are one body.

pl-l4d8c7-d1e146.summary: Quotes Augustine: the Church is called one bread and one body, since as one bread is made of many grains and one body of many members, the Church is joined of many faithful by charity. Christ consecrated this mystery of our peace and unity at his table; whoever receives the mystery of unity without holding the bond of peace receives it not for himself but against himself.
claims: The Church is made one by charity.
Receiving the sacrament of unity without peace is to one's harm.

pl-l4d8c7-d1e158.summary: Adds that Christ's own body from the Virgin is also a sacrament of the Church's unity: as his body consists of many pure members, the Church consists of many persons free of mortal stain, as figured by the ark made of incorruptible acacia wood.
claims: Christ's body is a sacrament of the Church's unity.

pl-l4d8c7.summary: Distinguishes the twofold reality of the eucharist: one contained and signified, Christ's flesh from the Virgin and the blood shed for us; the other signified and not contained, the unity of the Church in the predestined, called, justified, and glorified, Christ's mystical flesh, as Jerome distinguishes. So there are three things: sacrament only, the visible species; sacrament and reality, Christ's own flesh and blood; reality only, his mystical flesh. The species bears the likeness of both realities: as bread and wine nourish and gladden the body, Christ's flesh refreshes the inner man; and as one bread is made of many grains and wine of many grapes, the Church's unity is made of many faithful. Augustine: whoever receives the mystery of unity without the bond of peace receives it against himself. Christ's body from the Virgin is also a sacrament of the Church's unity, which consists of persons free from mortal stain, as the ark was made of incorruptible wood.
claims: The eucharist has a twofold reality: Christ's true flesh and blood, and the unity of the Church.
The visible species are sacrament only; Christ's body is sacrament and reality; the Church's unity is reality only.
The species signify both realities by likeness.
Receiving the sacrament without the bond of peace is to one's harm.
